x: Spanish j, pinyin h and Arabic خ are all [x]. Arabic خ is usually the strongest and scrapiest; Mandarin h is often lighter.
r: Spanish rr and Levantine ر are both trills. Arabic ر is often a tap between vowels, like Spanish single r.
gh: Spanish soft g is a gentle [ɣ]; Arabic غ is the same symbol but much stronger, almost a gargle.
pu: Spanish p and Mandarin b are the same sound: no puff. Mandarin p is the puffed [pʰ].
td: Spanish t/d and Arabic ت/د are dental, with the tongue on the teeth.
vi: A steady "ee" in all three languages, with no English glide.
vu: A real "oo" with rounded lips in all three.
ve: Spanish e and Levantine ē (as in بيت bēt) are close; neither glides like English "ay".
vo: Spanish o and Levantine ō (as in يوم yōm) are close; neither glides like English "oh".
